english_translation: Louis L. Bucciarelli, MIT, 2000; revised and annotated by Christine Blondel and Bertrand Wolff, 2012
original: Coulomb, First Memoir, memoir year 1785, printed 1788, pp.569–577, Plate XIII
images: Original public-domain 18th-century plate; extracted from supplied PDF. French scan checked for cosinus on p.576. English page facsimiles provided alongside the requested translation.

portrait.licence: Public domain, as marked on the Commons file description
portrait.note: Posthumous portrait/copy; not an eyewitness depiction of the 1785 experiment.

materials_note: Original text specifies the main instrument materials. Surface finish, brass appearance, workbench and lighting are an interpretive period setting. Paper scale, glass vessel, silver wire, shellac and pith spheres are represented distinctly.

stamp.source: Unaltered clean scan from Timbres de France; replaces user-provided Baidu-watermarked reference. No public-domain assertion.
stamp.depiction: Coulomb portrait and electric torsion balance; educational numbered overlays are separate HTML elements, not modifications to the supplied image

calibration: Modern fixed-arm tangential-force illustration; same material and length, kappa scales with wire diameter^4. Teaching assumptions: 1 degree readable step and 60 degree display window. Neither is a claimed historical detection limit or elastic failure angle. 2.5 degree zero offset is an illustration of the memoir's 2–3 degree discussion.
